solves: Gives a form choice a title and a short explanation of its consequence, with the whole card as the click area: a checkbox, a radio or a switch at its start, an optional icon and an optional shortcut. The same rich look, with a description below the label, is the rich option of the nph-select and nph-combobox list.
use_when: When each choice of a form needs a sentence that explains the consequence, such as a plan or a delivery method.
With control radio, for one choice among two to five that exclude each other.
With control checkbox, for several independent choices, each with its explanation.
With control switch, to turn a feature on or off with an immediate effect.
As the rich option of a list, with rich on nph-option, when the label alone is not enough to choose.
do_not_use_when: For a simple list of choices with no explanation: use nph-radio or nph-checkbox.
To mix controls in the same group: use only radios, only boxes or only switches.
With a shortcut on a card with a switch: the switch already acts on click.
For more than five exclusive choices: use nph-select, or nph-combobox above fifteen.
For an action that needs a button: the card chooses, it never runs a command.

control.constraint: The control the card holds, the Figma property `controle`. It reflects because the internal CSS and the radio group read it. checkbox for several choices, radio for one choice, switch for an on and off with an immediate effect. Any other value draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

checked.constraint: The current state, the Figma property `marcado`. The checked attribute is the initial state and the one form.reset() returns to; a later change of the attribute moves the current state only while neither the person nor code changed checked. Setting it from code unchecks the other cards of a radio group and fires no event. Checked changes only the control: the outline of the card does not change.

name.constraint: The group of a radio card and the key in the form. Radio cards with the same non-empty name, in the same root and with the same form owner, are one group. It reflects because the form reads the attribute of the host; an empty name writes no attribute. Without a name, a radio card is a group of one.

value.constraint: What a checked checkbox or radio card submits, under name. The default, on, is also written as the attribute. A card with a switch is not a form member and submits nothing, as nph-switch does; a card that is not drawn submits nothing.

text.constraint: The title, already localized; it is also the accessible name of the control, and it wraps. Without it the card draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

description.constraint: The second line, already localized: the consequence of the choice. It is the accessible description of the control. Empty turns it off.

icon.constraint: A core name of nph-icon, drawn light in an icon/size-md box after the control, in the color of the title. Empty turns it off. A name outside the core draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

shortcut.constraint: The keys of the shortcut hint, separated by spaces, each one in an nph-kbd at the end of the card. Empty turns it off. It is only a hint: the card binds no key. Never with control switch, which draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

keyShortcuts.constraint: The aria-keyshortcuts value, such as Meta+K (the attribute is key-shortcuts), written only when the product binds the key and calls the same action as the click. A disabled card announces none. Binding the key, and when it works, is the product's call.

invalid.constraint: The error outline. Visual only: aria-invalid is not supported on the radio and switch roles, and the sentence that says what to fix is the error message of the nph-field of the group. nph-field writes it on every card of the group. disabled wins over it.

disabled.constraint: The whole card at rich-option/disabled-opacity, out of the Tab order and the arrow keys, with no click. A disabled fieldset around the card does the same. It wins over invalid.

input.constraint: The native input event, fired on the host when the person checks or toggles the card: it bubbles and crosses the shadow root. Read event.target.checked. A change from code never fires it.

change.constraint: The native change event, fired on the host right after input, when the person checks or toggles the card: it bubbles and does not cross the shadow root. A change from code never fires it.

control.choose_when: radio for one choice among a few that need an explanation; checkbox for several independent choices; switch for an on and off with an immediate effect.
do_not_combine_with: Another control in the same group.

description.choose_when: On by default: a short sentence with the consequence of the choice. Off only when the title alone says everything.

icon.choose_when: When a symbol helps the person recognize the choice. Off by default.

shortcut.choose_when: When the product binds a key to the choice and wants it visible. Off by default.

default.changes_for_user: The card with its resting outline, inside the card, and the control at its default.

checked.changes_for_user: Only the control changes: the outline stays rich-option/border, and the choice reads by the control.

hover.changes_for_user: A layer under the content, with the corner of the card; the outline does not change. The control does not take its own hover from the card.

focus.changes_for_user: Keyboard only: the outline turns rich-option/focus-border and the halo shows outside the card. The control inside takes no ring of its own.

error.changes_for_user: The outline turns rich-option/border-error, checked or not; the control stays at default. With focus the outline stays the error one and the halo is the error one.

disabled.changes_for_user: The whole card loses opacity and stops responding. Checked keeps the checked control; error is not shown.

business_rules: The whole card is the click area: a click anywhere on it checks a radio card or toggles a checkbox or switch card.
The card holds the role, the state and the focus; the control inside is a visual indicator, inert and hidden from the screen reader.

Radio cards with the same name and the same form owner, in the same root, are one group: checking one unchecks the others, one Tab stop per group, and the arrow keys move the focus and check, wrapping.

Space checks a radio card and toggles a checkbox or switch card. Enter checks nothing on a checkbox or radio card, as nph-checkbox and nph-radio, and toggles a switch card, as nph-switch; it does not submit the form.
Only the person checking or toggling the card fires input and change; setting checked from code never fires them.
Only a checked checkbox or radio card enters the form, as name=value; a switch card is not a form member.
The shortcut is a hint: the card binds no key and sets aria-keyshortcuts only when keyShortcuts says the key is bound.
Hover only adds the layer: it never changes the outline. Error with hover keeps the error outline, focus with hover keeps the focus outline and the halo, and a disabled card takes no hover.
domain_errors: invalid: the group failed validation. Every card shows the rich-option/border-error outline; the sentence that says what to fix is the error message of nph-field.

tokens.outline: rich-option/border-width inside, rich-option/border; error rich-option/border-error; focus rich-option/focus-border
tokens.title: text/label-md in rich-option/foreground
tokens.description: text/caption in rich-option/description-foreground, rich-option/text-gap below the title
tokens.icon: nph-icon light in a rich-option/icon-size box, rich-option/foreground
tokens.control: nph-checkbox, nph-radio or nph-switch at the default size, inert
tokens.hover: rich-option/background-hover at rich-option/background-hover-opacity, a layer under the content

ai_hints: Use nph-rich-option when each choice needs a sentence that explains it; for a simple list, use nph-radio or nph-checkbox.
Use one control type per group: radio for one choice among two to five, checkbox for several, switch for an on and off.
Put the cards of a group inside an nph-field, which names the group and carries the error message; give the radio cards the same name and each one its value.
Write the title as the choice and description as the consequence, both already localized.
Read the choice from event.target.checked and event.target.value on change; do not listen to click.
Put checked on the default card; it is also the state the form returns to on reset.
Set invalid on every card of the group together with the error message of nph-field; never leave a card red without a sentence.
Do not put shortcut on a card with a switch, and set keyShortcuts only when the product binds the key.
For the rich option of a list, write rich and description on the nph-option; never write nph-rich-option inside a list.

accessibility.semantics: The host is the control: role checkbox, radio or switch, with aria-checked and aria-disabled, through ElementInternals. The control drawn inside is inert and aria-hidden. A group of radio cards inside nph-field is read as a group: see the known limits.
accessibility.accessible_name: The title is the name of the control (aria-label through the internals, because an id does not cross a shadow root) and the second line is its description (aria-description). The icon, the second line and the shortcut are hidden from the screen reader.
keyboard: Radio: Tab enters the group on the checked card or, with none checked, on the first one that responds; the next Tab leaves the group.
Radio: arrow down and arrow right move to the next card and check it, wrapping; arrow up and arrow left, to the previous one.
Checkbox and switch: each card is one Tab stop, and the arrows do nothing.
Space checks a radio card and toggles a checkbox or switch card.
Enter checks nothing on a checkbox or radio card and toggles a switch card, following the control held; it does not submit the form.
A disabled card is out of the Tab order and the arrow keys skip it.
accessibility.focus: Keyboard only: the outline turns rich-option/focus-border and a halo of rich-option/focus-ring-width shows outside the card; the control inside takes no ring. A mouse click does not show it.
accessibility.contrast: The title 19.56:1 in light and 12.45:1 in dark over rich-option/background, the second line 6.69:1 and 8.28:1. The resting outline is decorative; the boundary that meets 3:1 is the control inside. Known limit: in light mode of the default brand, focus/border measures 2.92:1 against the halo, as design.md records.
accessibility.color_alternative: The control says the choice, never the outline; the error has the sentence of nph-field.

invalid_combinations: A control outside checkbox, radio and switch — the card draws nothing.
An icon outside the core names — the card draws nothing.
A shortcut with the switch — the card draws nothing.
No text — the card draws nothing.
invalid with disabled — disabled wins: the error outline is not shown, and it is not a console error.
A radio card without name, or alone in its group — it renders as a group of one.
anti_patterns: Using the card for a simple list of choices with no explanation.
Mixing controls in the same group.
A shortcut on a card with a switch.
Treating the shortcut as a binding: the card binds no key.
A red card without a sentence that explains the error.
Painting the outline of the checked card: the control says the choice.
Writing nph-rich-option inside a list: the rich option of a list is nph-option with rich.
